os/signal#

Stopping cleanly on Ctrl-C (SIGINT), SIGTERM or SIGHUP.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let interruption = Interruption();
try {
    for files -> file {
        interruption.check();
        archive.add(file);
    }
}
catch e is Interrupted {
    archive.discard();
    return interruption.status();      // 130 after Ctrl-C, 143 after SIGTERM
}

Description#

Stopping cleanly on Ctrl-C (SIGINT), SIGTERM or SIGHUP.

Without an Interruption a signal ends the process at once, by the system's default action: nothing more of the program runs, so defer blocks and destroy do not either, and the shell sees the process killed by the signal.

An Interruption takes the signals from the moment it is made until it is closed or goes. The first one that comes is kept, and the program sees it at the points it chooses: check() throws Interrupted.signal(signal) there, so defer, destroy and catch handle it like any other failure. A long loop calls check() once per step:

An asynchronous program waits for it instead: await interruption.arrival().

Once one signal has come, the signals are given their earlier actions back, so a second Ctrl-C during the cleanup ends the process at once. status() is the conventional exit status of the signal that came, 128 and its number: 130 for interrupt, 143 for terminate, 129 for hangup.

Tests pass a source of their own, ManualSignals from testing/signal, and raise the signal themselves.
